## Problem Statement

Terminal session management is fragmented and opaque: users cannot simply manage default development and dedicated bot sessions or relocate tabs by category. Internal workspace IDs obscure native session names, logical groups do not move tabs, and automatic routing must respect manual choices and running work.

## Solution

First-class named terminal session CRUD, human-friendly discovery/current-context selection, persistent empty definitions, frozen bulk tab moves and conditional undo, composable categories and opt-in stable routing. Preserve process/conversation continuity, manual placement, exact identity and explicit failure outcomes across all public controller transports.

## User Stories

1. As an operator, I want to list recognizable terminal session names, backend, running/empty state, tab counts and health/activity summaries, so that I can choose a destination without opaque workspace IDs.
2. As an operator, I want to select by unique name or current terminal context, so that routine commands are simple.
3. As an script author, I want to receive structured ambiguity candidates instead of interactive prompts, so that automation never hangs.
4. As an operator, I want to create, inspect, edit, rename and delete terminal sessions, so that session management is complete.
5. As an operator, I want to retain an empty saved session without keeping agents alive, so that named destinations remain available.
6. As an operator, I want to discover existing native sessions without registration, so that default works immediately.
7. As an operator, I want to rename a session without changing its identity, so that rules continue targeting it correctly.
8. As an operator, I want to keep retired identities separate from reused names, so that old rules cannot act on replacement sessions.
9. As an operator, I want to edit descriptions, labels, directory, launch profile/command and display preferences, so that new tabs have useful defaults.
10. As an operator, I want to leave existing tabs unchanged when launch defaults change, so that running accounts and processes are preserved.
11. As an codex-bots user, I want to create or reuse a dedicated bots session, so that bot tabs stay separate from default development tabs.
12. As an codex-bots user, I want to avoid duplicating or restarting existing bots on session reuse, so that relaunch is predictable.
13. As an operator, I want to select explicit tabs, saved groups and arbitrary custom labels, so that I can organize work my way.
14. As an operator, I want to combine exact and pattern trait predicates with AND/OR/NOT, so that categories express real workflows.
15. As an operator, I want to treat unknown/stale traits as unknown unless explicitly selected, so that uncertain observations do not trigger unintended routing.
16. As an operator, I want to preview a frozen tab selection before moving it, so that I can inspect precisely what will change.
17. As an operator, I want to move whole tabs with panes, processes and conversations intact, so that running work continues.
18. As an operator, I want to retain focus by default during tab relocation, so that management does not interrupt my terminal.
19. As an operator, I want to see per-tab moved, failed, held and uncertain outcomes, so that partial batches remain understandable.
20. As an operator, I want to reconcile uncertain moves before retrying, so that commands never replay ambiguous effects blindly.
21. As an operator, I want to undo completed moves only when their resulting placement is unchanged, so that later manual decisions are respected.
22. As an operator, I want to hold routing after manual movement, explicit pins or undo, so that automatic rules do not fight me.
23. As an operator, I want to resume routing explicitly for selected tabs, so that I control when holds end.
24. As an operator, I want to save criteria and destination as prioritized routing rules, so that organization can be repeated or automated.
25. As an operator, I want to enable continuous routing per rule and include existing tabs explicitly, so that enabling a rule does not unexpectedly rearrange my current work.
26. As an operator, I want to require stable observations before routing, so that transient status changes do not cause tab churn.
27. As an operator, I want to resolve rules by priority and hold conflicting equal priorities, so that routing destinations are deterministic.
28. As an operator, I want to persist holds and reconcile unfinished operations after restart, so that recovery does not duplicate effects.
29. As an operator, I want to delete populated sessions only by explicitly draining or terminating their tabs, so that deletion has a clear effect.
30. As an operator, I want to retain a partially drained session and disable rules targeting deleted sessions, so that failures do not silently destroy or recreate destinations.
31. As an Windows or WSL caller, I want to use equivalent CLI/API/native MCP/OAuth MCP operations, so that platform entrypoints expose the same capabilities.
32. As an operator, I want to see unsupported psmux whole-tab cross-session movement before any effect, so that process restarts are never presented as moves.
33. As an operator, I want to use generated help and automatically installed Bash/Zsh completion, so that session commands are discoverable.

## Implementation Decisions

- Distinguish terminal sessions, tabs and agent conversations. Reuse existing controller tab ownership, durable operation journal, monitor, native adapters and saved views.
- Saved session identities survive native-container absence. Names are scoped to a terminal server; explicit qualifiers resolve ambiguity. Rename preserves identity; deleted identities cannot be silently rebound.
- New operations use the existing portable tab contract with generated CLI/help/completion and both MCP transports. Session-wide management uses an explicit management target; local same-user commands resolve it without manual grants. Existing resource-scoped grants must not become global management authority.
- Use a private durable session registry and bounded atomic writes/locks; discovered native sessions are visible before adoption. Defaults apply to new launches only; formatting preferences use the existing formatter's baseline/hold semantics.
- Freeze tab identities, source/destination identities and rule/selection revision in retained plans. Record each intended effect before dispatch, re-observe afterward, reconcile unfinished effects and preserve partial outcomes. No claim of atomic native bulk movement.
- Selectors support bounded composable JSON expressions and ordinary CLI flags, explicit tabs, named groups and custom labels. Unknowns do not match positive or negated ordinary comparisons unless explicitly selected.
- Continuous routing is opt-in, uses the existing bounded monitor, requires configurable stability, excludes existing tabs unless included explicitly, persists manual holds/pins and refuses equal-priority destination conflicts.
- Deletion requires explicit drain or terminate for populated sessions, retains failed/partial sessions, disables dependent routing rules only on confirmed deletion and retains history.
- First qualify WSL-hosted Byobu/tmux. Native psmux CRUD qualifies independently; whole-tab movement across psmux's separate servers remains unsupported, without restart/copy fallback.
- codex-bots launch integration creates/reuses its named destination and must not duplicate/restart existing bot processes simply on reuse. No automatic real bot launches in qualification.

## Testing Decisions

- Primary stable seam: public controller tab operations through ordinary CLI, real stdio MCP and authenticated HTTP/API/OAuth MCP, exercised with disposable private terminal namespaces.
- Focused public owner tests cover state/selector decisions cheaply; native tmux/psmux tests prove process/pane continuity, last-tab behavior, exact identity fences and readback. Reuse existing tab lifecycle, monitor, saved-view, portable-client and completion harnesses.
- Work vertically red then green; retain exact commands/first failures. Exercise partial failure, lost response, repeated intent, rename/name reuse, undo-after-manual-move, rule conflict, unknown traits and restart reconciliation.
- Local Python3.11/3.12 checks substitute for paid hosted GitHub CI. Installed immutable wheel equality ties final qualification to source. No provider prompts or production terminal effects.
- The accepted interview establishes public CLI/API/MCP parity and continuity as acceptance; no new competing test seam or architecture is introduced.

## Out of Scope

Windows-native service hosting, cross-host/cross-server process migration, psmux cross-session live movement, new Claude/Ollama harness adapters, conversation-copy substitution for moves, stock Codex changes, production activation, merge/deployment, paid hosted CI and unrelated terminal cleanup.

## Further Notes

All17 decisions were explicitly accepted during the design interview. Operator directs immediate ticket publication and implementation, primary owns one ticket, other ready tickets go one per worker. Close implementation tickets after integration-branch validation, then exactly one broad Standards/Spec review and one bounded TDD findings pass. Parent spec stays open. Frozen review base is the fetched origin/main commit at implementation start.
